name: publish-pilot-mcp

tools.name: preflight
tools.description: Check that git, gh and the registry CLI are installed, which accounts are logged in, and the git identity. Starts no logins. Run this first.

target.description: What to publish: a GitHub repo, a registry package, or both.

registry.description: Package registry: npm, pypi (PyPI) or crates (crates.io).

tools.name: install_tool
tools.description: Install a CLI tool with winget (Windows), brew (macOS) or apt (Linux). Known tools: git, gh, node, npm, python, cargo. After installing on Windows you may need to restart the MCP client so PATH updates.

tools.name: check_names
tools.description: Check that a package name is valid and free on the registry and that the GitHub repo name is free. When taken, returns the best free alternative (for npm, a scoped @user/name first).

registry.description: Package registry: npm, pypi (PyPI) or crates (crates.io).

packageName.description: Package name to check on the registry.

repoName.description: GitHub repo name to check under your account.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Start the browser-based login for github (gh auth login --web), npm (npm login --auth-type=web), pypi or crates. Returns at once with a job id, the one-time code and the URL; the user signs in, does 2FA and clicks Authorize. Poll job_status every 1–2 minutes until running is false.

service.description: Which account to log in to.

openBrowser.description: Open the login page in the default browser.

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Get the status and recent output of a login or publish job. Optionally wait up to waitSeconds for it to finish, or send Enter to it. Without an id, lists all jobs.

id.description: Job id from login, publish_package or setup_trusted_publishing.

waitSeconds.description: Wait up to this long for the job to finish. Capped at 45 s per call so the call returns before common 60 s client timeouts; call again while running is true.

sendEnter.description: Send Enter to the job (for 'Press ENTER' prompts).

stop.description: Stop the job (e.g. to restart a publish whose link expired).

tools.name: scaffold_project
tools.description: Create a standard project: source, tests, README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG, .gitignore, .gitattributes and a manifest (version 0.1.0, author from git config, repo URL, publishConfig for scoped npm). Adds CI and release workflows when repoUrl is set. For target 'repo' the README explains clone-and-build and the manifest blocks registry publishing; for private repos CI runs on Ubuntu only. Never overwrites existing files.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

registry.description: Package registry: npm, pypi (PyPI) or crates (crates.io).

cli.description: Add a command-line entry point with --help and --version (npm, pypi).

workflows.description: Default with repoUrl: ci+release for target 'both', ci+repo-release for 'repo', ci for 'package'.

target.description: What will be published. Default 'both' when repoUrl is set, otherwise 'package'.

private.description: The GitHub repo will be private: CI runs on Ubuntu only to save paid Actions minutes.

tools.name: add_workflows
tools.description: Write .github/workflows/ci.yml (install, lint, build, test on push and PR) and optionally release.yml (on v* tags: test, build, publish with trusted publishing via OIDC — skipped if the version exists — then a GitHub release from the CHANGELOG). Existing files are kept unless overwrite is true.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

release.description: registry: publish + GitHub release; github-only: just a GitHub release.

private.description: Private repo: CI runs on Ubuntu only (Windows minutes count 2x, macOS 10x).

tools.name: run_checks
tools.description: Run the project's install, lint, typecheck, build and test steps (npm scripts, a Python .venv with pytest + build, or cargo clippy/build/test). Stops at the first failure and returns its output.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

tools.name: scan_secrets
tools.description: Look for .env files, private keys and tokens in everything that would be committed. Reports file and line, never the secret itself.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

tools.name: inspect_package
tools.description: Run the registry dry run (npm pack/publish --dry-run, twine check, cargo publish --dry-run), list the files that would be published, and flag junk or secrets.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

tools.name: git_commit
tools.description: git init (branch main) if needed, refuse when secrets or .env files would be committed, then stage everything and commit.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

tools.name: create_github_repo
tools.description: gh repo create <name> --public|--private --source=. --push. Needs a commit and a GitHub login. If the repo already exists and is this folder's origin, just pushes.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

tools.name: publish_package
tools.description: Publish from the terminal (npm publish [--access public], twine upload, cargo publish). Skips when the version already exists, and for 24 hours after the registry answered E429 (retries can extend a rate-limit block). Returns a job; npm approval runs in a real terminal. If an approval link expires, call again.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

openBrowser.description: Open approval pages in the default browser.

force.description: Publish even within 24 hours of an E429. Only when the user confirms the block was lifted.

tools.name: setup_trusted_publishing
tools.description: Connect the package to the GitHub release workflow (OIDC, no stored tokens). npm: runs `npm trust github` (the user approves with 2FA) and returns the settings page as fallback. PyPI/crates.io: opens the settings page and returns the exact values to fill in. The user clicks Save.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

tools.name: tag_and_release
tools.description: Create tag v<version> from the manifest, push the branch and tag, and create the GitHub release with notes from CHANGELOG.md unless the repo's release.yml already does that on tags. Never moves or deletes tags.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

version.description: Must match the manifest; defaults to it.

createRelease.description: Default: create the release here only when .github/workflows/release.yml doesn't create one. Pass true or false to force.

tools.name: watch_workflow
tools.description: Wait for the workflow run (default release.yml) for the folder's current commit, optionally on a branch or tag, and report its result with the failing log on failure. Matching the commit avoids reporting an older run right after a push.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

ref.description: Only runs for this tag/branch, e.g. v0.1.1.

waitSeconds.description: Capped at 45 s per call so the call returns before common 60 s client timeouts; while the run is in progress, call again.

tools.name: bump_version
tools.description: Bump the manifest version (patch/minor/major) and record it in CHANGELOG.md: given notes become a new entry; without notes, a non-empty 'Unreleased' section becomes the new version. Does not commit.

dir.description: Project folder (absolute path, or relative to the server's working directory).

notes.description: Markdown for the CHANGELOG entry, e.g. '### Fixed\n\n- Release workflow.'

tools.name: verify_install
tools.description: In a brand-new temp folder, install the published package from the real registry (or git clone the repo, private ones included) and run the README's commands one by one, stopping at the first that fails. Installed executables are on PATH.

registry.description: Package registry: npm, pypi (PyPI) or crates (crates.io).

command.description: Commands to run in the folder (PowerShell on Windows, sh elsewhere). Prefer a list: each one must succeed before the next runs.

tools.name: notify
tools.description: Show a desktop notification, e.g. 'Ready for your approval'.

tools.name: open_url
tools.description: Open an https page on github.com, npmjs.com, pypi.org or crates.io in the default browser. Other hosts are refused.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Run a command line (PowerShell on Windows, sh elsewhere) and return its output, redacted of tokens. Destructive commands (force-push, deleting tags/repos/releases, unpublish, recursive delete) are refused.

instructions: publish-pilot takes a project from an empty folder to a published GitHub repo and/or npm, PyPI or crates.io package. Start with the publish_project prompt or call preflight. Long-running logins and publishes return a job id: poll it with job_status. Never enter passwords or 2FA codes for the user; leave sign-in, 2FA and Authorize/Approve/Save clicks to them.
